title: Trump Teleprompter Pays $170,000 to End Insider Trading Probe
summary: A White House teleprompter operator will pay more than $172,000 to end a federal regulator’s probe into alleged well-timed prediction market bets about President Donald Trump’s speeches.

title: Panama Canal Congestion Drives Gas Tankers to Unusual Routes
summary: Growing congestion at the Panama Canal is forcing some gas tankers into unusual journeys, from a rare detour around South America to the possible emergence of shuttling through the waterway.

title: Indian Bank Stocks Show Widest Exchange Price Gap in Decades
summary: Shares of some Indian banks closed at sharply different prices on the country’s two largest exchanges on Thursday, the latest sign of dislocation under the new closing auction system.

title: Wall Street Week | Debt & Consequences, Defying Fiscal Gravity, Hollywood Gets Democratized
summary: This week, Chrystia Freeland talks with the former finance ministers of the Netherlands and Germany about what it takes to bring spending under control. And, are US deficits now a bigger driver of interest rates than inflation? Plus, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his debut at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, we revisit the story of the wealthiest place in America. Later, the rise of YouTube filmmakers is democratizing discovery, while also flooding the market with more content than audiences can watch. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Former FDIC Chair Sheila Bair on Inflation, Regulatory Landscape
summary: Former FDIC Chair Sheila Bair discusses inflation and the regulatory landscape in an interview with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Two-Year Yield Jumps on Warsh’s Inflation Pledge: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street traders sent short-term yields sharply higher as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to bring inflation to the target, boosting bets on a rate hike and stabilizing longer-dated bonds.

title: India’s Mazumdar-Shaw Is On A Mission to Save Lives
summary:
Known as India’s ‘Queen of Biotech’, Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw built Biocon from a rented garage almost 50 years ago. Today, her multibillion-dollar company is one of the world’s biggest producers of insulin, and a leading force in biosimilars. 
As she looks at handing over her life’s work to successors, Mazumdar-Shaw talks to Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin about her pioneering journey as a female entrepreneur in India, her mission to deliver life-saving therapies to patients and what she believes India must do to tackle an AI future.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: IMF's Georgieva on Warsh's Speech, 'Stubborn' Inflation
summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh "did a great job" in his Jackson Hole speech. Speaking with Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz on "Bloomberg The Close." Georgieva also discusses recent inflation pressures and whether they reflect central bank failure or other forces. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran War Hits 6 Month Mark
summary: Bloomberg Businessweek looks back on the past six months of the US war with Iran, including how President Trump's timeline for the conflict has shifted as talks with Tehran remain mostly stalled. Bloomberg News White House and National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko discusses how the war has evolved, and what might come next. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Billionaire Gilinski, GeoPark Said to Be Near Venezuela Oil Deal
summary: Colombia’s richest family is nearing a Venezuela oil deal in conjunction with GeoPark Ltd, a Bogota-based oil company in which it is the largest shareholder with a 28% stake, according to people familiar with the matter who asked for anonymity discussing confidential plans.

title: Tariffs Could Bring Canada Auto "To Its Knees"
summary: President Trump vowed this week to hike tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel to 50% at the start of next year as part of an ongoing trade war threat with the country. Linda Hasenfratz, Executive Chair of Linamar, says that after decades of free trade in automotives between he US and Canada, the implementation of such high tariffs would "cripple the industry." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: What’s Behind the Classic Jackson Hole Photo Op?
summary: For years, the Fed chair would give an address in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and Wall Street and news organizations wouldn't have a recent photo of the chair to accompany stories. In steps Bloomberg's own Mike McKee. Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal and Tom Keene learn the origin of the now traditional "Fed perp walk." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Passes 160 Per Dollar to Hit Weakest Level in a Month
summary: The yen moved past 160 per US dollar to its weakest level in a month, extending a slide that’s erased more than half of its intervention-fueled gains.

title: Por qué EE.UU. está detrás de una parte del petróleo de Venezuela
summary: Aunque Venezuela ya no es la gran potencia petrolera que fue en el pasado, el país cuenta con algunas de las mayores reservas de petróleo del mundo. Desde que Estados Unidos destituyó al entonces presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro el 3 de enero, ha restablecido las relaciones diplomáticas y está colaborando con el gobierno de la presidenta interina Delcy Rodríguez en Caracas. title: The Science Behind The Markets | Masters in Business with David Booth
summary: Barry speaks with David Booth, founder and chairman at Dimensional Fund Advisors and author of Stay Calm. They discuss his time at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business where he was the research assistant to American economist and Nobel Laureate Eugene Fama, before leaving to start Dimensional Fund Advisors. They discuss embracing the uncertainty of the markets and the importance of staying the course. David also discusses his philanthropic history and giving back to the places that shaped him.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Threat of a Fed Rate Hike Is Changing the Leadership in Markets, Slimmon Says
summary: Andrew Slimmon, managing director and head of applied equity advisors at Morgan Stanley, says he's happy with what Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said during his speech at Jackson Hole and he remains consistent. Slimmon says the threat of an interest rate hike is causing a change in leadership in stock markets. He shares more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Funds Add Bullish Gasoline Bets at Fastest Pace in Six Months
summary: Hedge funds boosted their bullish wagers on US gasoline by the most since the US-Iran war began, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data showed.

title: Mexico Sells Samurai Bond for First Time in Two Years
summary: Mexico returned to the Samurai bond market for the first time in two years on Friday, raising ¥282.8 billion ($1.77 billion) amid a rush of issuance as borrowers seek to lock in funding before Japanese interest rates potentially climb further.

title: US Stocks Close Lower After Warsh Speech | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Lisa Mateo and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Americans Feel Guilty About Spending Money on Fun
summary: Bloomberg's  Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Almost three-quarters of US adults feel guilty when they spend on things that bring them joy instead of putting the money toward their financial goals. (Source: Bloomberg)
